title: UPDATE: US Chip Producer Prices Surge 27% as AI Data Centers Squeeze Supply
summary:
US producer prices for semiconductors and electronic parts climbed 27% from a year earlier, hovering near a June peak of 27.6% that surpassed the previous high set in 1980, as AI data centers absorb component supply. Memory prices have jumped 245% over the past year, and research firm IDC forecasts the average smartphone price will increase 27.6% to $581 this year as chipmakers charge device manufacturers more.

The component surge accompanies a broader acceleration in the September Producer Price Index, which rose 1.3% from August and 6.3% from a year ago, topping consensus estimates of 0.6% and 5.4% for the largest monthly and annual gains since 2022. Final demand goods prices jumped 2.6% on the month, the biggest increase since the Bureau of Labor Statistics began tracking the series in December 2009, led by a 10.8% surge in energy costs as wholesale diesel rose 21%, gasoline climbed 20.3% and grains gained 17%. Core PPI, which excludes food and energy, increased 0.7% on the month and 5% over the past year, beating forecasts of 0.3% and 4.4%.

selectedTweets.text:
🦔Wholesale prices jumped 1.3% in September, more than double what economists expected, and are up 6.3% from a year ago. At the producer level, diesel rose 21% in a single month and grains rose 17%. Retail sales grew 0.8%, but nearly all of that came from people paying more for gas.

My Take
I’d treat this report as a preview of the grocery bill, unfortunately. Diesel moves almost every truckload of food in the country, and grain feeds the cattle and chickens, so I expect food prices in the consumer numbers to keep climbing through the holidays. Retailers and wholesalers also widened their margins 1.4% last month, so some of this is businesses charging more than their own costs went up.

Strip out gas and retail sales rose just 0.2% while consumer prices rose 0.6%, so people are buying less and paying more for it. The Fed raised rates in September, and a report like this makes another hike before year end very likely. That keeps mortgage and credit card rates high for families who are already pulling back.

Hedgie🤗
